passage:
Our social studies group had four people making a chart about rivers. Sangeeta kept saying, "You're so good at this, you'll finish anyway," and drew doodles in her notebook. She did the same on Monday and Tuesday. On Wednesday the teacher stopped by and looked at the pile of pages, all in Aarav's and Farida's handwriting. Sangeeta went red and looked at the floor. After the bell she said, "I've been slack. Give me the map and the title, and I'll do them tonight." Aarav shrugged. Next day the map was done, coloured carefully. I can't say why she changed; maybe it was the teacher's look.

- Gopika

qa.q: Which parts did Sangeeta ask for after the bell?
What might Sangeeta have been feeling when the teacher looked at the pages and she went red?
qa.a: Embarrassed or guilty, perhaps because the pages were all in other people's handwriting, though Gopika says she can't be sure why Sangeeta changed.

qa.q: What could Sangeeta do to keep her share fair for the rest of the project?
qa.a: Take a real task from the start, check in with the group, and say so if she slips.

qa.q: How might Aarav and Farida have felt while Sangeeta doodled?
qa.a: Probably tired and unappreciated doing all the pages, though the passage only shows Aarav shrugging when she offered to help.

grounding: A child lets others do the work assuming they will finish anyway, then admits being slack and takes a real share, seen by a group mate.

passage:
The science project was due in two days, and the power kept cutting out in Darshan's building. That was his excuse for not doing his part.
Sonali and the others had been working at her house every evening. "Darshan, did you finish the chart?"
"No light at my place," he said. Which was true, sort of. But he'd played games on his phone instead.
He thought Sonali would do it anyway. She always did.
That night Sonali messaged the group, exhausted. "I can't do everything."
Darshan felt a hot rush of shame. The next morning he said, "I've been slack. I'll do the chart tonight, by candlelight if I have to."

qa.q: What was Darshan supposed to make?
How did Darshan feel after Sonali's message?
qa.a: He felt a hot rush of shame, realising he had taken advantage of her.

qa.q: What did Darshan do that was honest?
qa.a: He admitted he had been slack and promised to do his share, even by candlelight.

qa.q: How might Sonali feel doing all the work?
qa.a: Sonali was exhausted and overwhelmed, messaging that she couldn't do everything.

grounding: A boy lets others do the project, thinking they will anyway; seeing a group mate exhausted, he admits he was slack and takes a real share.

passage:
The group project on rivers had been going for a week in the Pune school library. Tenzin had done nothing. Every time the group met, he said, "You guys are better at this," and drew in his notebook.
Pradeep had done the map, the rivers list and half the chart. Today he looked tired. "Tenzin, could you at least write the introduction?"
Tenzin shrugged. "You'll do it better."
Pradeep put down his pen. "That's not fair. It's your project too."
Tenzin felt his face go hot. Pradeep was right.
"Sorry. I've been lazy. I'll do the intro and the conclusion tonight."

qa.q: What had Pradeep done for the project?
qa.a: The map, the rivers list and half the chart.

qa.q: How did Tenzin feel when Pradeep said it wasn't fair?
qa.a: He felt ashamed, his face going hot.

qa.q: What did Tenzin do once he saw his slackness?
qa.a: He apologised, admitted he had been lazy and took on the introduction and conclusion.

qa.q: How might Pradeep feel about Tenzin's apology?
qa.a: Pradeep would likely feel relieved and respected.

grounding: A boy lets his group do the work; when a group mate calls it unfair, he admits being lazy and takes a real share.
